exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Row Operation That's Equivalent To Left Multiplication by an Elementary Matrix

question.text: Let $E = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ gives the result of the product $EA.$
question.explanation:
The matrix $E$ is obtained by taking the first row of the identity matrix and adding $-9$ times the second row:

\begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &:= R_1 + (- 9)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E \end{align*}

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the row operation $R_1:=R_1 - 9R_2$ to $A.$

question.explanation:
The matrix $E$ is obtained by taking the second row of the identity matrix and adding $-5$ times the first row:

\begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 := R_2 + (-5) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E. \end{align*}

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the row operation $R_2 := R_2 + (-5) R_1$ to $A.$

question.text: Suppose we are applying the elementary row operation $R_1:= 18R_1$ to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A.$ Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
question.explanation:
We need to find an elementary matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation $R_1:= 18R_1$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

\begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1& := 18R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E \end{align*}

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{bmatrix} 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\cdot A \]

question.text:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

\[ R_2 := -2 R_2 ,\qquad R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2, \qquad R_2 := R_2 + 3R_1 \] Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
question.explanation:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations.

  • The first elementary row operation is $R_2 := -2 R_2.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 := -2 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second elementary row operation is $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 &\leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

  • The third elementary row operation is $R_2 := R_2 + 3R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 := R_2 + 3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_3 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 0& 1 \\ 1& 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ 0& -2 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to $E_2E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_3$ on the left and get $E_3E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ 3& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0& 1 \\ 1& 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ 0& -2 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

question.text:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

\[ R_1 := \dfrac12R_1 ,\qquad R_2 := R_2 + R_1 \qquad R_1 := R_1 + 4R_2 \] Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
question.explanation:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the three given elementary row operations.

  • The first elementary row operation is $R_1 := \dfrac12R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} &R_1 := \dfrac12R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac12 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second elementary row operation is $R_2 := R_2 + R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 := R_2 + R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

  • The third elementary row operation is $R_1 := R_1 + 4R_2 .$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 := R_1 + 4R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_3 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ 1& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{2}& 0 \\ 0& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to $E_2E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_3$ on the left and get $E_3E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 4 \\ 0& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ 1& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{2}& 0 \\ 0& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

question.text:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

\[ R_1 := -\dfrac{1}{4}R_1,\qquad R_2 :=R_2+(-2)R_1, \qquad R_2 :=\dfrac{1}{5}R_2 \] Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
question.explanation:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the three given elementary row operations.

  • The first elementary row operation is $ R_1 := -\dfrac{1}{4}R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 := -\dfrac{1}{4}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{1}{4}& 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second elementary row operation is $ R_2 :=R_2+(-2)R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 :=R_2+(-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

  • The third elementary row operation is $ R_2 :=\dfrac{1}{5}R_2.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 :=\dfrac{1}{5}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac{1}{5} \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_3 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ -2& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to $E_2E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_3$ on the left and get $E_3E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ 0& \dfrac{1}{5} \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1& 0 \\ -2& 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

question.text:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

\[ R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2, \qquad R_2 := R_2 + 5R_1 ,\qquad R_2 := 6R_2 \] Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
question.explanation:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations.

  • The first elementary row operation is $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_1 \end{align*}

  • The second elementary row operation is $ R_2 := R_2 + 5R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 := R_2 + 5R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_2 \end{align*}

  • The third elementary row operation is $R_2 := 6R_2.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: \begin{align*} I &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 := 6R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= E_3 \end{align*}

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0& 1 \\ 1& 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to $E_2E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_3$ on the left and get $E_3E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0& 1 \\ 1& 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot A \]
